items.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I’ll be touring with Chick Corea this summer. He’s putting together a tribute to Bud Powell. We’re going to go out with a group...

ctx.x: Tell us about the new record coming out in just a few days.

Yeah the new record is called “Number Two Express” and I’m so excited, I’m so excited, because you know the new album represents me where I am now musically — things I like to listen to and things I like to go for and the things that I would like to eventually have the band get into. You know I’ve always been about diversity. You know you can’t be in just one bag. And I try to make a conscious effort for my band to play you know lots of blues and some progressive stuff maybe some things leaning to a funk, and…

bag so they’ll know what it’s all about. And you know on the new album I have Chick Corea playing acoustic and electric piano and one of the best things about that was him and Jack DeJohnette got to play together again, because Jack is on the album also. And they hadn’t worked together. They told me they’d maybe played together maybe three or four times since 1969. And it was such a thrill for me to have them record on my new CD. And Kenny Garret is on it as well playing alto saxophone. And on the other half of…

items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s one of the few bassists I can think of, including Christian, too, Christian McBride... John can cover all the musical bases, like Stanley can.

ctx.x: So the ‘70s progress, the ‘80s progress, we don’t have to get into all the minutiae... But at a certain point, you start linking up with the bassist who was your primary bass partner after Stanley Clarke, John Patitucci, with whom you do a number of things over a decade. That also seems like an important link. I know you also encouraged him to strike out on his own after a certain point. Can you describe that relationship.

Around ‘82 or ‘83, I started to want to form another group that had an electric sound to it, so I could write music kind of in the direction of Return to Forever, but with a new set of musicians. We were living in L.A. at that time, and my wife Gayle and I would put on Valentine’s parties... Gayle loves hearts and valentines, and so we would host a Valentine’s party in L.A., and invite musicians and friends, just to come over. Gayle would always promote jamming during the evening. At that time, I was looking for…
